newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX falters on weak Wall St, dollar.
newsitem.headline: German DAX falters on weak Wall St, dollar.

text.p: The dollar's sharp slide from last week's highs against the mark and Friday's decline on Wall Street weighed on German shares on Monday but the firm Bund market preserved the market from a significant sell-off.

The 30-share DAX index ended the bourse session at 4,333.13 points, down 21.02 points or 0.5 percent. But that marked a firm recovery from lows hit in pre-bourse electronic dealings, when the IBIS DAX sank to a low of 4,267.74 points.
Dealers said a steady performance on the Bund market helped stabilise the equity market. Isolated gains on selected stocks also helped buoy the broader market.

A mega-merger in the Swiss financial services sector between Credit Suisse and insurer Winterthur fired renewed interest in shares in Commerzbank AG, which repeatedly comes into the spotlight as a takeover target.
Commerzbank co-operates with Winterthur in Germany and the merger revived talk it might be taken over from Switzerland.
"The rumour mill is grinding again," said one Frankfurt dealer.
Commerzbank led volumes throughout the session and ended at 69.10 marks, up 2.55 marks or nearly four percent.
Among the other winners were steelmakers Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp and Thyssen AG after the influential Spiegel magazine said the two allied groups were intensifying merger talks.
Krupp rose eight marks, or 2.5 percent, to 328 marks, while Thyssen rose 11 marks, or 2.7 percent, to 424 marks.
Tyre-maker Continental hit a new high of 50.20 marks before closing up three percent at 49.70 after reporting its six-month earnings rose 73 percent to 208 million marks.

On the downside, shares in pharmaceuticals group Altana AG plunged as the company confirmed market speculation that it had ceased developing a successor to its Pantoprazol stomach ulcer drug. Analysts said this would have minimal impact on earnings in the mid-term but could be negative in the longer term.
Altana dropped 43.50 marks, or 23 percent to 143.50 marks.
